finding.claim: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in /dl. The user-supplied filename is joined to the root with filepath.Join, which only cleans the path and does not confine it. A '../' sequence escapes /srv/files and the file contents are returned to the caller.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (r.URL.Query().Get("f")), unauthenticated and attacker-controlled
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", leaving the root. Join does not reject '..'.
The file contents are written back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check against root, no filepath.Base, no rejection of '..' or absolute components, no os.Root or fs.ValidPath use, and no authentication or authorization on the route. The URL decoder lets %2e%2e%2f through. Go's ServeMux path cleaning only affects the URL path, not the query string, so it does not help. The /avatar handler is not affected because filepath.Base strips directory components.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw query param f into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no containment check, and files.go:32 registers /dl bare with no auth, so ../../etc/passwd is read and written back at files.go:18.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw query param 'f' to filepath.Join("/srv/files", name), which only cleans the path so "../../etc/passwd" escapes the root, and files.go:18 writes the contents back with no auth, prefix check or Base() on /dl (files.go:32).
